title: Ethical Hacking for Defenders
summary: Learn how attackers work, inside a simulated lab, so you can detect, fix and report what they find. Starts with law and ethics.
description: Start with authorization, written scope and coordinated disclosure, then play the attacker's role (including how output encoding stops XSS) only against toy, in-process targets: a simulated network, canned logs, made-up banners and synthetic samples. For every offensive idea you write the detection, the fix or the finding report. Nothing here touches a real system, and nothing in the course may be used against a system you do not own or lack written permission to test. Continue with controlled offensive testing: replay authorization matrices, confirm path traversal with synthetic markers, and prove mass assignment through fresh state reads.
outcomes: Assess simulated vulnerabilities and write actionable findings within an authorised lab.
Design controlled offensive probes and distinguish confirmed impact from misleading responses.
